requirements.quote:
The Decision Process selects routes for subsequent advertisement by
   applying the policies in the local Policy Information Base (PIB) to
   the routes stored in its Adj-RIBs-In.  The output of the Decision
   Process is the set of routes that will be advertised to peers; the
   selected routes will be stored in the local speaker's Adj-RIBs-Out,
   according to policy.
requirements.condition: When selecting routes for subsequent advertisement
requirements.required_behavior: Apply local Policy Information Base policies to routes stored in Adj-RIBs-In.
requirements.why_checkable: The route selection inputs and resulting routing-table state provide a concrete check.

requirements.quote:
The BGP Decision Process described here is conceptual, and does not
   have to be implemented precisely as described, as long as the
   implementations support the described functionality and they exhibit
   the same externally visible behavior.
requirements.condition: When implementing the conceptual BGP Decision Process
requirements.required_behavior: Support the described functionality and exhibit the same externally visible behavior; the exact internal implementation may differ.
requirements.why_checkable: Externally visible route-selection and advertisement behavior can be compared with the described process without requiring identical internal organization.

requirements.quote:
The selection process is formalized by defining a function that takes
   the attribute of a given route as an argument and returns either (a)
   a non-negative integer denoting the degree of preference for the
   route, or (b) a value denoting that this route is ineligible to be
   installed in Loc-RIB and will be excluded from the next phase of
   route selection.
requirements.condition: When evaluating a given route with the conceptual route-selection preference function
requirements.required_behavior: Take the given route's attribute as the function argument.
requirements.why_checkable: The preference calculation inputs can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
The selection process is formalized by defining a function that takes
   the attribute of a given route as an argument and returns either (a)

   installed in Loc-RIB and will be excluded from the next phase of

requirements.condition: When the preference function assigns a degree of preference to a route
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the degree of preference as a non-negative integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The assigned preference value can be checked for type and lower bound.

requirements.quote:
The selection process is formalized by defining a function that takes
   the attribute of a given route as an argument and returns either (a)
   a non-negative integer denoting the degree of preference for the
   route, or (b) a value denoting that this route is ineligible to be
   installed in Loc-RIB and will be excluded from the next phase of
   route selection.
requirements.condition: When the preference function returns the route-ineligible value
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the route as ineligible for installation in Loc-RIB.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Install that ineligible route in Loc-RIB.
requirements.why_checkable: The route selection inputs and resulting routing-table state provide a concrete check.

requirements.quote:

requirements.required_behavior: Exclude that route from the next phase of route selection.
requirements.why_checkable: The route selection inputs and resulting routing-table state provide a concrete check.

requirements.quote:
The function that calculates the degree of preference for a given
   route SHALL NOT use any of the following as its inputs: the existence
   of other routes, the non-existence of other routes, or the path
   attributes of other routes.  Route selection then consists of the
   individual application of the degree of preference function to each
   feasible route, followed by the choice of the one with the highest
   degree of preference.
requirements.condition: When calculating the degree of preference for a given route
requirements.forbidden_behavior: SHALL NOT use the existence of other routes as an input.
requirements.why_checkable: The calculation dependencies can be inspected and preference compared while other routes are introduced.

requirements.condition: During route selection
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the degree-of-preference function individually to each feasible route.
requirements.why_checkable: The route selection inputs and resulting routing-table state provide a concrete check.

requirements.quote:
The function that calculates the degree of preference for a given
   route SHALL NOT use any of the following as its inputs: the existence
   of other routes, the non-existence of other routes, or the path
   attributes of other routes.  Route selection then consists of the
   individual application of the degree of preference function to each

requirements.condition: After individually applying the degree-of-preference function to each feasible route
requirements.required_behavior: Choose the route with the highest degree of preference.
requirements.why_checkable: The selected route's preference can be compared with those of competing feasible routes.

requirements.quote:
a) Phase 1 is responsible for calculating the degree of preference
         for each route received from a peer.
requirements.condition: In conceptual Phase 1 of the Decision Process, or an implementation with equivalent externally visible behavior
requirements.required_behavior: Calculate the degree of preference for each route received from a peer.
requirements.why_checkable: The route selection inputs and resulting routing-table state provide a concrete check.

requirements.quote:
b) Phase 2 is invoked on completion of phase 1.  It is responsible
         for choosing the best route out of all those available for each
         distinct destination, and for installing each chosen route into
         the Loc-RIB.
requirements.condition: On completion of conceptual Phase 1, or the equivalent processing in an implementation with the same externally visible behavior
requirements.why_checkable: The route selection inputs and resulting routing-table state provide a concrete check.

requirements.quote:
b) Phase 2 is invoked on completion of phase 1.  It is responsible
         for choosing the best route out of all those available for each
         distinct destination, and for installing each chosen route into
         the Loc-RIB.
requirements.condition: In conceptual Phase 2, or an implementation with equivalent externally visible behavior
requirements.required_behavior: Choose the best route out of all available routes for each distinct destination.
requirements.why_checkable: The route chosen for each destination can be checked against the available candidates.

requirements.quote:
b) Phase 2 is invoked on completion of phase 1.  It is responsible
         for choosing the best route out of all those available for each
         distinct destination, and for installing each chosen route into
         the Loc-RIB.
requirements.condition: When a route is chosen in conceptual Phase 2, or equivalent processing
requirements.required_behavior: Install each chosen route in Loc-RIB.
requirements.why_checkable: The route selection inputs and resulting routing-table state provide a concrete check.

requirements.quote:
c) Phase 3 is invoked after the Loc-RIB has been modified.  It is
         responsible for disseminating routes in the Loc-RIB to each
         peer, according to the policies contained in the PIB.  Route
         aggregation and information reduction can optionally be
         performed within this phase.
requirements.condition: After Loc-RIB has been modified, in the conceptual Decision Process or an implementation with equivalent externally visible behavior
requirements.why_checkable: The route selection inputs and resulting routing-table state provide a concrete check.
